0.why: Regex.cpp:90 reads this jack with getVoltage, channel 0 only, into a dsp::TSchmittTrigger left at Rack's defaults of 1V high and 0V low. Every sequence starts its own reset from that edge, at RegexSeq-process.cpp:33 in clock mode and :94 in pitch mode, and a sequence's own reset jack is added on top rather than replacing it. Regex.cpp:70 returns from process on any sample whose frame number is not a multiple of eight, so this jack is only looked at once every eight samples and a pulse shorter than that can pass unseen.

comment: The second jack of a line and the line's main output are left without a family on purpose: in clock mode they are triggers and in pitch mode they carry volt-per-octave pitches, so no one colour is true of either. The Bias input is named Orientation in the maker's tooltip and Bias on the panel and in the manual. The module declares twelve sets of jacks and parameters whatever the model; on Regex only the first eight have widgets. A parameter between the mode switches and the Bias knob is declared and never read (PARAM_BIAS_DEPTH in Regex.hpp), and has no widget. The whole module is processed once every eight engine samples (REGEX_FRAME_DIVIDER), so a pulse shorter than that can be missed. Regex Condensed is the same module with all twelve lines given widgets and less room on screen for each expression.
